Subject: Post-call: model evals & multilingual checks for EU/APAC

Hi Anna / Satoshi —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap:
- Objective: narrow down a short list of models and an evaluation plan to validate locale-specific quality across your EU (DE/FR/ES) and APAC (JP/KR) storefronts.
- Current priority: customer-facing product descriptions and post-purchase support routing (high precision required for DE/FR/ES + JA/KO).
- Constraints: on-prem data residency for EU pilot; procurement timeline target: end of June.

Proposed next steps (recommendation):
1) Redwood to deliver: per-locale benchmark (automated + human spot-check) using your sample prompt set. We’ll run the baked-in multilingual evals and share a summarized report.
2) Shortlist models: 3 model variants (small/medium/large) with quantization profiles and cost/latency estimates.
3) Pilot plan: 2-week pilot on Dedicated capacity for 1 EU and 1 APAC locale, with acceptance criteria (per-locale accuracy thresholds + latency SLO).
4) Procurement: we’ll provide a draft SOW and a procurement checklist for your legal/IT.

I attached the post-call notes and an initial prompt set (globex_prompt_set_v2.csv). Can you confirm the priority languages and whether you want DE/FR/ES in the same evaluation or staged?

I’ll also circulate suggested models and a Drive link to the raw benchmark outputs by tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: RE: Post-call: model evals & multilingual checks for EU/APAC — technical notes

Hi all —

Quick technical notes and a couple of risk items for the evaluation so expectations are aligned: 

1) JA / KO quality regressions: we often see models optimized on mostly English data underperform on Japanese/Korean when evaluation focuses on character-level correctness or honorifics. For product descriptions we should run both automatic metrics (chrF, BLEU) and human QA for real-world acceptance.

2) Tokenization / normalization: for German compounds and French contractions, we’ll add locale normalization steps and compare pre-tokenized vs. raw to measure drift.

3) Fallback & routing policy: recommend configuring a language-detection gate + highest-confidence fallback to a smaller, cheaper model for low-latency use cases, and strong fallback to redwood-llama-70b-q4 for generation tasks when confidence thresholds are not met. This reduces hallucination risk.

4) Data residency: for the EU Dedicated pilot we’ll use a private control plane and ensure the KV-caching policy avoids persisting customer content beyond the pilot window. Procurement will want a short security appendix describing caching and encryption-at-rest/key management.

Attached is the preliminary automated benchmark PDF with per-locale summaries (multilingual_benchmark_results_Q1_2027.pdf). I flagged a few JA/KO examples with notable regressions — we should do a small human-labeling pass on ~200 samples to quantify.

Metrics we’ll report:
- Intent classification: precision/recall/F1 per locale
- Generation: chrF, BLEU, and 5-point human quality score (accuracy/fluency/legal-accuracy)
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95) under your sample QPS

I’ll kick off the JA/KO tokenizer checks later today and share an initial report by EOD Monday.

-Neha
